{"ok": true, "path": "solvers/deutils.py", "start_line": 94, "end_line": 140, "total_lines": 273, "truncated": false, "content": "94:def ode_order(expr, func):
95:    """
96:    Returns the order of a given differential
97:    equation with respect to func.
98:
99:    This function is implemented recursively.
100:
101:    Examples
102:    ========
103:
104:    >>> from sympy import Function
105:    >>> from sympy.solvers.deutils import ode_order
106:    >>> from sympy.abc import x
107:    >>> f, g = map(Function, ['f', 'g'])
108:    >>> ode_order(f(x).diff(x, 2) + f(x).diff(x)**2 +
109:    ... f(x).diff(x), f(x))
110:    2
111:    >>> ode_order(f(x).diff(x, 2) + g(x).diff(x, 3), f(x))
112:    2
113:    >>> ode_order(f(x).diff(x, 2) + g(x).diff(x, 3), g(x))
114:    3
115:
116:    """
117:    a = Wild('a', exclude=[func])
118:    if expr.match(a):
119:        return 0
120:
121:    if isinstance(expr, Derivative):
122:        if expr.args[0] == func:
123:            return len(expr.variables)
124:        else:
125:            args = expr.args[0].args
126:            rv = len(expr.variables)
127:            if args:
128:                rv += max(ode_order(_, func) for _ in args)
129:            return rv
130:    else:
131:        return max(ode_order(_, func) for _ in expr.args) if expr.args else 0
132:

821:def classify_ode(eq, func=None, dict=False, ics=None, *, prep=True, xi=None, eta=None, n=None, **kwargs):
822:    r"""
823:    Returns a tuple of possible :py:meth:`~sympy.solvers.ode.dsolve`
824:    classifications for an ODE.
825:
826:    The tuple is ordered so that first item is the classification that
827:    :py:meth:`~sympy.solvers.ode.dsolve` uses to solve the ODE by default.  In
828:    general, classifications at the near the beginning of the list will
829:    produce better solutions faster than those near the end, thought there are
830:    always exceptions.  To make :py:meth:`~sympy.solvers.ode.dsolve` use a
831:    different classification, use ``dsolve(ODE, func,
832:    hint=<classification>)``.  See also the
833:    :py:meth:`~sympy.solvers.ode.dsolve` docstring for different meta-hints
834:    you can use.
835:
836:    If ``dict`` is true, :py:meth:`~sympy.solvers.ode.classify_ode` will
837:    return a dictionary of ``hint:match`` expression terms. This is intended
838:    for internal use by :py:meth:`~sympy.solvers.ode.dsolve`.  Note that
839:    because dictionaries are ordered arbitrarily, this will most likely not be
840:    in the same order as the tuple.
841:
842:    You can get help on different hints by executing
843:    ``help(ode.ode_hintname)``, where ``hintname`` is the name of the hint
844:    without ``_Integral``.
845:
846:    See :py:data:`~sympy.solvers.ode.allhints` or the
847:    :py:mod:`~sympy.solvers.ode` docstring for a list of all supported hints
848:    that can be returned from :py:meth:`~sympy.solvers.ode.classify_ode`.
849:
850:    Notes
851:    =====
852:
853:    These are remarks on hint names.
854:
855:    ``_Integral``
856:
857:        If a classification has ``_Integral`` at the end, it will return the
858:        expression with an unevaluated :py:class:`~.Integral`
859:        class in it.  Note that a hint may do this anyway if
860:        :py:meth:`~sympy.core.expr.Expr.integrate` cannot do the integral,
861:        though just using an ``_Integral`` will do so much faster.  Indeed, an
862:        ``_Integral`` hint will always be faster than its corresponding hint
863:        without ``_Integral`` because
864:        :py:meth:`~sympy.core.expr.Expr.integrate` is an expensive routine.
865:        If :py:meth:`~sympy.solvers.ode.dsolve` hangs, it is probably because
866:        :py:meth:`~sympy.core.expr.Expr.integrate` is hanging on a tough or
867:        impossible integral.  Try using an ``_Integral`` hint or
868:        ``all_Integral`` to get it return something.
869:
870:        Note that some hints do not have ``_Integral`` counterparts. This is
871:        because :py:func:`~sympy.integrals.integrals.integrate` is not used in
872:        solving the ODE for those method. For example, `n`\th order linear
873:        homogeneous ODEs with constant coefficients do not require integration
874:        to solve, so there is no
875:        ``nth_linear_homogeneous_constant_coeff_Integrate`` hint. You can
876:        easily evaluate any unevaluated
877:        :py:class:`~sympy.integrals.integrals.Integral`\s in an expression by
878:        doing ``expr.doit()``.
879:
880:    Ordinals
881:
882:        Some hints contain an ordinal such as ``1st_linear``.  This is to help
883:        differentiate them from other hints, as well as from other methods
884:        that may not be implemented yet. If a hint has ``nth`` in it, such as
885:        the ``nth_linear`` hints, this means that the method used to applies
886:        to ODEs of any order.
887:
888:    ``indep`` and ``dep``
889:
890:        Some hints contain the words ``indep`` or ``dep``.  These reference
891:        the independent variable and the dependent function, respectively. For
892:        example, if an ODE is in terms of `f(x)`, then ``indep`` will refer to
893:        `x` and ``dep`` will refer to `f`.
894:
895:    ``subs``
896:
897:        If a hints has the word ``subs`` in it, it means that the ODE is solved
898:        by substituting the expression given after the word ``subs`` for a
899:        single dummy variable.  This is usually in terms of ``indep`` and
900:        ``dep`` as above.  The substituted expression will be written only in
901:        characters allowed for names of Python objects, meaning operators will
902:        be spelled out.  For example, ``indep``/``dep`` will be written as
903:        ``indep_div_dep``.
904:
905:    ``coeff``
906:
907:        The word ``coeff`` in a hint refers to the coefficients of something
908:        in the ODE, usually of the derivative terms.  See the docstring for
909:        the individual methods for more info (``help(ode)``).  This is
910:        contrast to ``coefficients``, as in ``undetermined_coefficients``,
911:        which refers to the common name of a method.
912:
913:    ``_best``
914:
915:        Methods that have more than one fundamental way to solve will have a
916:        hint for each sub-method and a ``_best`` meta-classification. This
917:        will evaluate all hints and return the best, using the same
918:        considerations as the normal ``best`` meta-hint.
919:
920:
921:    Examples
922:    ========
923:
924:    >>> from sympy import Function, classify_ode, Eq
925:    >>> from sympy.abc import x
926:    >>> f = Function('f')
927:    >>> classify_ode(Eq(f(x).diff(x), 0), f(x))
928:    ('nth_algebraic',
929:    'separable',
930:    '1st_exact',
931:    '1st_linear',
932:    'Bernoulli',
933:    '1st_homogeneous_coeff_best',
934:    '1st_homogeneous_coeff_subs_indep_div_dep',
935:    '1st_homogeneous_coeff_subs_dep_div_indep',
936:    '1st_power_series', 'lie_group', 'nth_linear_constant_coeff_homogeneous',
937:    'nth_linear_euler_eq_homogeneous',
938:    'nth_algebraic_Integral', 'separable_Integral', '1st_exact_Integral',
939:    '1st_linear_Integral', 'Bernoulli_Integral',
940:    '1st_homogeneous_coeff_subs_indep_div_dep_Integral',
941:    '1st_homogeneous_coeff_subs_dep_div_indep_Integral')
942:    >>> classify_ode(f(x).diff(x, 2) + 3*f(x).diff(x) + 2*f(x) - 4)
943:    ('factorable', 'nth_linear_constant_coeff_undetermined_coefficients',
944:    'nth_linear_constant_coeff_variation_of_parameters',
945:    'nth_linear_constant_coeff_variation_of_parameters_Integral')
